name: David Fattal
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2019-2025); Hurun Global (2020-2026)
forbes_bio: David Fattal founded Fattal Hotels, Israel's largest hotel organization.
Fattal got his start as a waiter and bellboy and rose through management ranks before starting Fattal Hotels in 1998 at age 41.
He took the chain's parent company, Fattal Holdings 1998, public on the Tel Aviv Stock Exchange in 2018.
The company owns 47 hotels in Israel with 9,000 rooms, and manages 255 hotels with a total of more than 50,000 rooms across Israel, Europe and the Mediterranean region.
Fattal owns about 51% of Fattal Holdings and nearly 9% of Mediterranean Towers, which is also listed on the Tel Aviv Stock Exchange.

name: Chaitanya Desai
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026)
forbes_bio: Chaitanya Desai is the managing director of Mumbai-based Apar Industries.
The 68-year-old company manufactures conductors, electric cables, speciality oils, polymers and lubricants.
His older brother Kushal is chairman and managing director of Apar Industries.
Apar was originally called Power Cables when it was set up in 1958 by his late father Dharamsinh Desai.
forbes_facts: His mother Maithili Desai hails from the Mafatlal family, an old textile clan in Mumbai.

name: Sunil Vaswani
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2021); Forbes annual (2016-2020); Hurun Global (2016-2023); Sunday Times Rich List (2020); Wikidata (2021)
forbes_bio: Sunil Vaswani's Dubai-headquartered Stallion Group, named after his favorite animal, gets the bulk of its $4 billion in revenue from Africa.
Stallion's businesses span commodities trading, frozen foods, auto assembly and dealerships, including Nissan, Volkswagen, Audi and Porsche.
Vaswani is expanding Stallion's African footprint with a $9 billion investment in sectors such as steel, petrochemicals and agriculture.
forbes_facts: A British and Nigerian citizen, Vaswani was born in India, grew up in Nigeria and went to college in London.
Vaswani lives in Dubai's tony Emirates Hills in an opulent mansion, which includes an indoor aviary, a nightclub, an automatic car wash and a casino.

name: B.R. Shetty
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2020); Forbes annual (2014-2019); Hurun Global (2014); Wikidata (2016)
forbes_bio: Former pharma salesman B.R. Shetty immigrated from Karnataka in south India to Abu Dhabi in 1973 to set up a healthcare empire.
His biggest asset is London-listed NMC Health, one of the UAE's largest hospital chains.
In May 2019, Shetty listed Finabir, the holding firm for his money remittance firms UAE Exchange and Travelex Group.
Shetty also owns healthcare firm BR Life, which has a presence in India, Nepal, Africa and the Gulf region.
Shetty's son Binay is chief executive of BRS Ventures, the family's holding company.
forbes_facts: Shetty is funding a $150 million movie on the Hindu epic the Mahabharata, which will be India's most expensive film.
He owns the entire 100th floor of Dubai's Burj Khalifa, the world's tallest skyscraper.
In May 2018, Shetty signed the Giving Pledge.

name: Rick Workman
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026)
forbes_bio: Rick Workman is the founder and chairman of Heartland Dental, the largest dental support organization in the U.S. with more than 1,900 offices in 39 states.
He founded Heartland in 1997 after selling a 29 office practice that same year for $15.8 million.
Private equity giant KKR took a 58% stake in Heartland in 2018 at a $2.8 billion valuation.
In 2024, Heartland had $3.6 billion in revenue and $455 million in earnings.
In 2025, became a minority owner of the Tampa Bay Rays major league baseball team.
forbes_facts: Raised on a farm in Clay County, Illinois. Comes from a family of farmers and teachers. His mother was one of his grade school teachers.

name: Trevor Burgess
sec_insider_companies: Neptune Insurance Holdings Inc. (NP) - CEO & Chairman of the Board
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Hurun Global (2026); SEC insider holdings (2026)
forbes_bio: Trevor Burgess is chairman and CEO of flood insurance company Neptune Insurance Holdings.
Burgess owns nearly a third of the company, which went public on the New York Stock Exchange in October 2025.
Neptune Insurance Holdings is the largest private flood insurance company in the US. Burgess joined the company as its controlling shareholder and a director in 2018 and was named CEO in 2019.
Burgess previously served as CEO of a publicly-traded bank called C1 Financial, which was acquired by Bank of the Ozarks in 2016. At C1, he became the first openly gay CEO of a publicly traded bank.
Before joining C1 in 2012, Burgess worked as an investment banker at Morgan Stanley for  nearly a decade.

name: Zhang Xinghai

name: Justin Rosenstein
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2022); Hurun Global (2022); Hurun Global U40 (2022); Hurun Unicorn founders (2019-2020)
forbes_bio: Justin Rosenstein cofounded project management software company Asana with Facebook cofounder Dustin Moskovitz in 2008.
Asana went public via direct listing in September 2020 and Rosenstein now owns approximately 25% of the company's stock.
Rosenstein served as president of the company for eight years before stepping down in 2019. He still sits on Asana's board.
Rosenstein previously worked as a product manager and engineer at Google and Facebook, where he met Moskovitz and co-created the "like" button.
Rosenstein was featured prominently in the documentary "The Social Dilemma" as a vocal critic of social media's harmful effects.
forbes_facts: Rosenstein cofounded One Project, a nonprofit focused on equitable, ecological and effective governance and economics in communities around the world, in 2019.
Rosenstein's Asana and big data analytics company Palantir, cofounded by fellow Facebook alum Peter Thiel, went public via direct listing on the same day.

name: Brendan Blumer
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2026); Hurun Global (2026); Hurun Global U40 (2026); Wikidata; SEC insider holdings (2026); Hurun Unicorn founders (2019-2022)
forbes_bio: Brendan Blumer is cofounder of Hong Kong-based crypto exchange Bullish.
Bullish was founded in 2020 and went public on the New York Stock Exchange in August 2025.
Blumer owns a 28% stake in the company and serves as a director. Another Bullish board member, Kokuei Yuan, owns 25% of the company and is also a billionaire.
Blumer is also CEO and sole owner of block.one, a digital asset investment firm he cofounded in 2016. Bullish was majority-owned by block.one until 2024.
Blumer grew up in Iowa and moved to Hong Kong in 2005. He gave up his U.S. citizenship in 2020.

name: Svein Stole
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2020); Forbes annual (2017-2019); Hurun Global (2020)
forbes_bio: Former business journalist Svein Støle is the owner of Pareto Group, a financial services conglomerate.
The company provides financing, research and asset-management services to such clients as foundations, pension funds and high-net-worth individuals.
Through Pareto's shipping arm it also manages tankers, dry bulk ships and drilling rigs.
Støle worked as a journalist for Norwegian business publication Kapital before taking a job as an analyst at an investment bank in 1987.
In 1992 he and a group of investors bought Pareto, then a small project finance and securities outfit of bankrupt Oslobanken.
forbes_facts: He reportedly bought his first bond in high school.

name: Roman Avdeev
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2012-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026)
forbes_bio: Avdeev's first business was selling radio components and decoders for TV sets in the late 1980s.
The source of his wealth is Credit Bank of Moscow, one of Russia's largest banks by assets, which Avdeev bought in 1994 responding to a newspaper ad.
In addition to the financial sector, Avdeev owns a pharmacy chain and has assets in construction, timber and oil industries.
He sold all his assets including Credit Bank of Moscow to his partner billionaire Sergei Sudarikov in 2024.
Avdeev founded the charitable foundation "Arithmetic of Good," which helps orphans.
forbes_facts: Avdeev has 23 children, 19 of whom are adopted.
In 2009, Avdeev ascended Mount Wilson, Antartica's highest point.
Avdeev owns football club Torpedo, founded in the early 1920s on the basis of the sports department of the Red Army

name: Mu Rongjun
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2020-2025); Hurun Global (2020-2026); Hurun China (2018-2026); Hurun Global U40 (2020); Hurun China U40 (2019-2020)
forbes_bio: Mu Rongjun is a cofounder, an executive director and a senior vice president of Meituan Dianping, the Yelp equivalent in China.
Before cofounding the company, Mu worked as a senior software engineer and project manager at Baidu, China's dominant search engine, for two years.
Mu also cofounded fanfou.com, a social media company specializing in microblogging, where he worked as an engineering director for two years.
